absent: Locking discipline for concurrent page table reads and updates.
Allocation, freeing and reference counting of page table pages.
TLB invalidation primitives and barrier ordering beyond caller selected flags.
Fault handling, permission overlay key management and VMA interaction.
Concrete numeric values and bit positions of PTE flag and address fields.
MTE hardware tag transfer granule and folio flag lifecycle details.

findings.text: Page table raw values share one 64 bit unsigned carrier with distinct aliases per level and protection. Each level has its own alias name but identical width and representation.

Each page table entry and protection value is wrapped in a single member structure holding only its raw value, giving type separation between leaf, intermediate and protection values while preserving direct value conversion.

The vmalloc area starts at the modules end and ends before the vmemmap area with a guard gap. One variant subtracts a fixed gap from vmemmap start, another adds unused vmemmap capacity derived from address size difference. The vmemmap pointer maps physical start to page descriptors by linear offset.
Lazy MMU mode has three operations: entry does nothing, flush emits PTE barriers only if a pending thread flag was set and clears it, and exit simply performs the flush operation.

Range TLB maintenance is specialized by level with distinct granule and level parameters for PMD versus PUD. Spurious fault repair uses page or PMD range invalidation restricted to local, non notifying behavior, with an extra no walk cache qualifier for the PMD form. Bad PTE reporting logs location and raw value.

Physical address translation from PTE exists in two configurations: one masks and reassembles low and shifted high address fields after clearing a sharing related bit, with inverse packing on the return path, and a simpler one masks only the low address field and returns identity on the return path.

Leaf predicates inspect individual status bits: empty means zero value, young reflects access flag, special and write and read only and user reflect their named flags, user execution reflects absence of unprivileged execute never, tagged reflects a specific attribute index encoding, and contiguity requires both valid and cont bits.

Software versus hardware dirty are distinguished: software dirty is an explicit flag, hardware dirty means writable and not read only, and overall dirty is their disjunction. Accessibility uses present when a TLB flush is pending and valid otherwise.

Contiguous range helpers cap an address range at the next contiguous block boundary for PTE and PMD granules using wrap safe comparison. Leaf size helpers report the contiguous size when the cont bit is set and the base granule size otherwise.

User access permission without overlay requires both valid and user bits plus writability when a write is requested. The full check additionally consults a permission overlay key extracted from the entry. Block level checks convert the block entry to PTE view and reuse the same test.

Write and dirty state transitions preserve software dirty across permission changes: making writable clears read only only if already software dirty, making clean sets read only and clears software dirty, making dirty sets software dirty and clears read only if writable, and write protect first captures hardware dirty into software dirty before clearing write and setting read only. Age and special and cont transitions toggle only their named bit.

PMD bit set and clear operate by OR and AND NOT with a protection mask. Kernel valid conversion clears a present invalid encoding and sets a kernel valid encoding. Cont and section conversions set only cont or section type bits while preserving the remaining value.

User fault fd markers exist in present and swap encodings with test, set and clear operations. Setting the present marker also applies write protection. Swap exclusive has analogous set, test and clear operations that affect only its dedicated bit.

Debug only PTE update checking warns when a live valid to valid update clears the young bit, clears dirty while the old entry was writable, or makes an attribute change deemed unsafe. It skips invalid endpoints and largely private address spaces.

Live kernel attribute updates without break before make allow only a limited flag subset and allow creation or removal unconditionally. They forbid page frame changes and non global to global promotion, while permitting interchange between normal and normal tagged memory types.

Installation time synchronization first synchronizes instruction and data caches for present user executable non special entries, then synchronizes MTE tags when MTE is supported and the entry is user accessible, non special and tagged. Tag synchronization initializes hugetlb folios once and normal pages per page, followed by a write barrier before PTE visibility.

Cache maintenance exports synchronize a folio backing a PTE only once per clean flag, choose between aliasing and non aliasing invalidation sequences for a range, and provide a point of unification clean that reduces to an ordered barrier when cache hierarchy acceleration is present.

Level conversion helpers reinterpret the same raw value across page, middle, upper and global directory types in both directions, and PTE frame advance adds a page count to the frame number while preserving protection. PTE protection extraction is an identity style accessor.
Protection none uses a distinctive present invalid encoding that is additionally privileged and non executable for both privileged and user execution. The PMD form delegates the test to its PTE view.

Most PMD and PUD predicates and mutators delegate to the corresponding PTE operation on a converted view and convert back, covering young, write, user, execution, protection, dirty handling, age, validity and fault markers. Huge block formation sets section type without altering validity so present invalid inputs stay present invalid. Emptiness means zero value and bad means not a table.

Batched installation dispatches table checking by granule size for page, PMD and PUD, synchronizes caches and tags once for the whole batch scaled by stride, then iterates validating safety and writing each slot while advancing the frame number, and completes with a post write barrier. Single PMD and PUD stores are one element batches.

Protection constructors replace the memory type and execute controls while preserving other bits: no execute adds privileged execute never, non cached and write combine and device and DMA coherent select their device or normal non cacheable encodings with both execute never bits, tagged selects normal tagged, and decrypted versus encrypted toggle a shared namespace bit.
The maximum huge TLB state count is four, and the default huge page granule is the PMD granule with size, mask and order derived from it.
Attribute safety evaluation and tag synchronization are externally visible helpers used during mapping updates and PTE installation.
